author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two men face charges after a Cranston traffic stop led police to seize suspected methamphetamine, prescription pills and drug paraphernalia, according to the department’s account reported by NBC 10 WJAR.

Police said the stop occurred around 4:44 p.m. Monday on Wentworth Avenue. Officers allegedly saw drug paraphernalia in plain view and searched the vehicle, recovering about 30 grams of a substance that field-tested positive for methamphetamine, along with pills, a scale, a pipe and $90.

The driver was identified as Brandon Pierpont, 33, of Bellingham, Massachusetts, and the passenger as Miguel Rodriguez, 28, of Cranston. Police said both had active domestic-violence warrants. Pierpont also had a New Hampshire extradition warrant tied to narcotics charges.

Pierpont faces several drug-related counts, including possession with intent to deliver, while Rodriguez was charged with obstructing an officer and transferred to Woonsocket police. The allegations and field-test result will be subject to the court process; charges do not establish guilt, and laboratory testing may be used to confirm the substance.
dek: Police say a vehicle search produced about 30 grams of suspected methamphetamine, prescription pills and drug paraphernalia.
headline: Two face charges after Cranston traffic-stop drug seizure
